name: Cross-Dimensional Residual Frequency Compensation
definition: A frequency-domain compensation scheme that targets high-frequency details difficult to fit in the spatial domain, aiming to overcome inherent blurring artifacts of Gaussian kernels.
summary: Cross-Dimensional Residual Frequency Compensation mitigates Gaussian kernel blurring by extracting high-frequency rendering residuals, filtering them in the frequency domain, and injecting the energy directly into primitive attributes.
